Support Vector Machines · Margins06

SVMs in Biology

Golub et al. (1999) measured the activity of about 7,000 genes in samples from 72 leukemia patients and asked: can we tell the two main types (AML and ALL) apart from the genes alone?

That's thousands of features and only dozens of samples, so infinitely many lines separate the training data perfectly and most of them are bad.

Picking the line with the largest   is a sensible way to choose, and SVMs (Furey et al., 2000) became one of the standard tools for classifying tumors from gene activity.

Support Vector Machines · Margins07

Hard-Margin vs. Soft-Margin SVMs

Hard-Margin SVMs allow no misclassifications, much like a Perceptron

Soft-Margin SVMs allow for some misclassifications to allow for a more robust decision boundary

Support Vector Machines · Kernels22

Matching: Support Vector Machines

  MarginA. Allows some misclassifications for a more robust decision boundary
  Support vectorsB. The gap between the decision boundary and the closest points of each class
  Hard-margin SVMC. Allows no misclassifications, much like a Perceptron
  Soft-margin SVMD. Fast and simple, but only finds a straight-line (hyperplane) boundary
  Lagrangian multipliersE. Builds very complex boundaries from distances; needs tuning of γ and C
  Kernel trickF. Computes dot products in a higher-dimensional space without transforming the data
  Linear kernelG. Finds curved boundaries of a chosen degree; can overfit at high degrees
  Polynomial kernelH. The points on or inside the margin that define the decision boundary
  RBF kernelI. Wrap the "s.t." constraints into a single cost/error/loss function
